s401.content:
Anthony became a monk on Mount Athos and returned to Kyiv, where he lived as a hermit in a cave on the hills above the Dnieper River. Disciples gathered around him and dug more caves.

From this beginning grew the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, the Monastery of the Caves, the great center of monastic life in Ukraine. He is honored as the father of monasticism in the lands of Rus’.
s401.intercession: St. Anthony of the Caves, pray for us. Teach us to seek God in silence and prayer. Amen.

s402.content:
Theodosius left his wealthy family as a young man to join St. Anthony in the caves of Kyiv. As abbot he organized the growing community under the rule of the Studite monks of Constantinople.

He was known for his humility, wearing coarse clothing and doing the hardest work himself, and for his care for the poor and sick of Kyiv. He is a founder, with Anthony, of the Kyiv Caves Monastery.
s402.intercession: St. Theodosius, pray for us. Make us humble servants of our brothers and sisters. Amen.

s403.content:
Sabbas was born in Cappadocia and became a monk in the Judean desert under St. Euthymius. In 483 he founded the Great Lavra in the Kidron valley near Jerusalem, now called Mar Saba, which is still inhabited by monks today.

He led the monks of Palestine, defended the Council of Chalcedon, and journeyed to Constantinople in old age to plead for his people. The monastic rule of Mar Saba shaped Byzantine worship for centuries.
s403.intercession: St. Sabbas, pray for us. Bless all monks, and teach us to pray with the whole Church. Amen.

s404.content:
Euthymius was an Armenian priest from Melitene who went to the Holy Land and spent the rest of his life in the Judean desert, founding communities of monks.

He converted many Arab tribesmen and baptized their chief. He was the spiritual father of St. Sabbas, and his loyalty to the Council of Chalcedon helped keep the monks of Palestine faithful to its teaching about Christ.
s404.intercession: St. Euthymius, pray for us. Make us faithful to the true teaching about Christ. Amen.

s405.content:
Athanasius was a teacher in Constantinople who became a monk. With the help of the emperor Nikephoros Phokas, he founded the Great Lavra on Mount Athos in 963, the first great monastery on the Holy Mountain.

Mount Athos became the heart of Byzantine monasticism. Athanasius died when the dome of a church under construction collapsed on him and several of his monks.
s405.intercession: St. Athanasius, pray for us. Bless the monks of the Holy Mountain, and all who seek God in prayer. Amen.

s406.content:
Demetrius was a young Christian, by tradition a soldier and a deacon, who taught the faith in Thessalonica during the persecution of the emperor Maximian. He was arrested and killed with spears.

His tomb became a famous pilgrimage site, and the people of Thessalonica believed he defended their city from attack. He is one of the most beloved military saints of the East.
s406.intercession: St. Demetrius, pray for us. Defend the defenseless, and give us courage to confess Christ. Amen.

s407.content:
Panteleimon was a young physician in Nicomedia, the son of a pagan father and a Christian mother. Converted by a priest named Hermolaus, he healed the sick freely in the name of Christ.

Jealous doctors denounced him during the persecution of Diocletian, and he was beheaded. He is honored in the East as one of the "Unmercenary Healers" and a patron of physicians.
s407.intercession: St. Panteleimon, pray for us. Heal the sick, and bless all who care for them. Amen.

s408.content:
John was a widower from Cyprus who became Patriarch of Alexandria. He called the poor of the city "my lords and masters," kept a list of them, and gave so much that he died with almost nothing.

He built hospitals and homes for the poor and sheltered refugees fleeing the Persian invasion of the Holy Land. The Knights Hospitaller took him as their first patron.
s408.intercession: St. John the Merciful, pray for us. Teach us to see Christ in the poor and to share all we have. Amen.

s409.content:
Nilus was a Greek-speaking monk from Calabria in southern Italy, where Byzantine Christianity flourished. He founded several monasteries and was famous for his learning and his fearless counsel to emperors and popes.

At the end of his life he founded the Abbey of Grottaferrata near Rome, which still celebrates the Byzantine liturgy in full communion with the pope today.
s409.intercession: St. Nilus, pray for us. Bless the Italo-Albanian Church, and help East and West to live as one. Amen.

s410.content:
Gregory was an Armenian monk and poet who lived at the monastery of Narek. His Book of Lamentations, ninety-five prayers "speaking with God from the depths of the heart," is the treasure of Armenian literature.

Armenians have long kept it by the beds of the sick. In 2015 Pope Francis declared him a Doctor of the Church.
s410.intercession: St. Gregory of Narek, pray for us. Teach us to speak to God from the depths of our hearts. Amen.

s411.content:
Mariam Thresia was a Syro-Malabar laywoman and mystic from Kerala, India. She visited the sick and the dying, cared for the poor of every caste, and helped troubled families.

In 1914 she founded the Congregation of the Holy Family to continue this work. She bore the marks of Christ’s Passion and suffered greatly in prayer. She was canonized in 2019.
s411.intercession: St. Mariam Thresia, pray for us. Bless families, and help us to care for those in need around us. Amen.

s412.content:
Rani Maria was a Franciscan Clarist sister of the Syro-Malabar Church who worked among the poor landless villagers of Madhya Pradesh, helping them escape exploitation by moneylenders.

In 1995 a hired killer stabbed her to death on a crowded bus. Her family later forgave and embraced her killer, who repented. She was beatified as a martyr in 2017.
s412.intercession: Blessed Rani Maria, pray for us. Give us courage to defend the poor, and the grace to forgive. Amen.

s413.content:
Augustine Thevarparampil, called Kunjachan, "little father," was a short and humble Syro-Malabar priest in Kerala. He spent his life among the Dalits, the poorest and most despised people of the caste system.

He visited their homes, taught them the faith, and baptized thousands. He was beatified in 2006 as an apostle of the poor.
s413.intercession: Blessed Kunjachan, pray for us. Help us to love those whom society rejects. Amen.

s414.content:
The three Massabki brothers were Maronite laymen of Damascus: Francis, a married silk merchant and father of eight, Abdel-Mooti, a teacher, and Raphael. During the massacre of Christians in July 1860, they took refuge in the Franciscan friary.

Offered their lives if they would become Muslims, they refused and were killed together with eight Franciscan friars. They were canonized in 2024.
s414.intercession: Holy Massabki brothers, pray for us. Strengthen persecuted Christians in the Middle East. Amen.

s415.content:
Estephan was a brother of the Lebanese Maronite Order who spent most of his life working in the gardens and fields of the monastery of Kfifan, where St. Nimatullah is buried.

He was known for his gentleness and for the words he often repeated: "God sees me." He was beatified in 2010.
s415.intercession: Blessed Estephan, pray for us. Help us to work quietly in the presence of God. Amen.

s416.content:
Mykolai was a Ukrainian Greek Catholic Redemptorist priest and seminary teacher, consecrated bishop to serve Ukrainian Catholics in Volhynia and Polissia.

Arrested by the Soviets in 1945, he endured years of interrogation and labor camps. Released near death, he died in Lviv in 1959. He was beatified in 2001.
s416.intercession: Blessed Mykolai, pray for us. Strengthen pastors who suffer for their flocks. Amen.

s417.content:
Josaphat was a Basilian monk and the Ukrainian Greek Catholic bishop of Przemyśl. After the Second World War, the Soviet and Polish communist authorities moved to destroy his Church.

He was arrested, handed over to the Soviets, and died in a labor camp near Kyiv in 1947. He was beatified in 2001.
s417.intercession: Blessed Josaphat, pray for us. Keep the Church faithful in times of persecution. Amen.

s418.content:
Klymentiy was a nobleman and lawyer, brother of Metropolitan Andrey Sheptytsky, who became a Studite monk and archimandrite. During the Nazi occupation he helped hide Jews in monasteries and convents.

Arrested by the Soviets in 1947, he died in Vladimir prison in 1951. He was beatified in 2001 and recognized by Yad Vashem as Righteous Among the Nations.
s418.intercession: Blessed Klymentiy, pray for us. Give us courage to protect the persecuted. Amen.

s419.content:
Fr. Mykola Konrad was a Ukrainian Greek Catholic priest and teacher, and Volodymyr Pryjma the cantor and choir director of his parish in Stradch.

In June 1941 they went together to hear the confession of a sick woman. On their way home they were seized by Soviet secret police and killed in the woods. Both were beatified in 2001.
s419.intercession: Blessed Mykola and Volodymyr, pray for us. Make us faithful in bringing Christ to the sick and dying. Amen.

s420.content:
Olha Matskiv entered the Sisters Servants of Mary Immaculate and took the name Tarsykia. She offered her life to God for the conversion of those persecuting the Church.

In July 1944, when she answered the door of the convent in Krystynopil, a Soviet soldier shot her dead. She was twenty-four. She was beatified in 2001.
s420.intercession: Blessed Tarsykia, pray for us. Help young people to offer their lives generously to God. Amen.

s421.content:
Olympia was a Ukrainian Greek Catholic Sister of St. Joseph who led her community in Khyriv. When the Soviets arrested her and her sisters, she kept them together in prayer.

Deported to Siberia, she continued to pray and teach the faith among the prisoners until she died of illness in 1952. She was beatified in 2001.
s421.intercession: Blessed Olympia, pray for us. Keep us faithful in exile and suffering. Amen.

s422.content:
Petro was a Ukrainian Greek Catholic priest who served Ukrainian Catholics in Berlin and was named apostolic visitor for Ukrainians in Germany.

When Soviet forces took Berlin in 1945, he was arrested and sentenced to labor camps in Siberia, where he died in exile in 1957. He was beatified in 2001.
s422.intercession: Blessed Petro, pray for us. Bless all who serve immigrants and people far from home. Amen.

s423.content:
Ivan was a Ukrainian Greek Catholic Redemptorist priest and seminary professor. After the communist authorities outlawed his Church, he continued to lead his community in secret.

Arrested in 1950, he was savagely beaten on Good Friday in a Siberian labor camp and died weeks later. He was beatified in 2001.
s423.intercession: Blessed Ivan, pray for us. Unite our sufferings with the Passion of Christ. Amen.

s424.content:
Andrii was a Ukrainian Greek Catholic priest, a professor of canon law at the Lviv Theological Academy, and a parish priest in the village of Sykhiv.

When Soviet troops retreated in June 1941, he refused to abandon his parishioners and was killed by soldiers. He was beatified in 2001.
s424.intercession: Blessed Andrii, pray for us. Make shepherds faithful to their people in every danger. Amen.

s425.content:
Pavol was a Basilian monk and the Slovak Greek Catholic bishop of Prešov. He protected Jews during the Second World War and was later recognized by Yad Vashem as Righteous Among the Nations.

When the communists outlawed his Church in 1950, he refused to break with Rome. He was sentenced to life in prison and died in Leopoldov prison on his seventy-second birthday. He was beatified in 2001.
s425.intercession: Blessed Pavol Peter, pray for us. Keep us faithful to the successor of Peter whatever the cost. Amen.

s426.content:
Metod was a Czech Redemptorist priest who adopted the Byzantine rite to serve Greek Catholics in Slovakia. He led missions and cared for the faithful during the war.

Arrested by the communists in 1950, he was imprisoned for years and died in Leopoldov prison after being punished for singing a Christmas carol. He was beatified in 2001.
s426.intercession: Blessed Metod, pray for us. Help us to sing God’s praises in every circumstance. Amen.

s427.content:
Vasil was the auxiliary bishop of the Greek Catholic eparchy of Prešov in Slovakia. When the communists suppressed his Church, he was imprisoned for thirteen years and tortured.

Released in poor health, he helped rebuild the Greek Catholic Church during the Prague Spring of 1968. He died of the effects of his imprisonment and was beatified in 2003.
s427.intercession: Blessed Vasil, pray for us. Give hope to all who rebuild the Church after persecution. Amen.

s428.content:
In 1948 the communist government of Romania outlawed the Romanian Greek Catholic Church and imprisoned its bishops for refusing to join the state-controlled Orthodox Church.

Seven bishops died in prison or under house arrest, among them Iuliu Hossu of Cluj-Gherla, whom Pope St. Paul VI named a cardinal in secret. Pope Francis beatified all seven at Blaj in 2019.
s428.intercession: Blessed martyr bishops of Romania, pray for us. Strengthen the Church in her unity and freedom. Amen.

s429.content:
Justin was an Italian Vincentian priest sent to Ethiopia in 1839. He learned the language and customs of the people and adopted the ancient Ge’ez liturgy rather than imposing Latin customs.

As bishop he trained Ethiopian priests and laid the foundations of the Ethiopian Catholic Church. He died on a roadside while traveling to his people and was canonized in 1975.
s429.intercession: St. Justin de Jacobis, pray for us. Bless the Churches of Ethiopia and Eritrea, and teach us to respect every culture. Amen.

s430.content:
Moses was raised in Pharaoh’s court, fled to Midian, and met God in the burning bush on Mount Horeb. God sent him to lead Israel out of slavery in Egypt, through the Red Sea, and across the desert for forty years.

On Mount Sinai he received the Law and the covenant. He died within sight of the Promised Land, and he appeared with Elijah beside Christ at the Transfiguration. The Church honors him as the greatest of the prophets of the Old Covenant.
s430.intercession: Holy Moses, friend of God, pray for us. Lead us out of every slavery and teach us to keep God’s commandments. Amen.

s431.content:
Elijah defended the worship of the one true God in the northern kingdom of Israel against the cult of Baal promoted by King Ahab and Queen Jezebel. On Mount Carmel he called down fire from heaven before the prophets of Baal.

Fleeing for his life, he heard God at Horeb not in the wind or the earthquake or the fire, but in a still small voice. He was taken up to heaven in a fiery chariot, and he appeared with Moses at the Transfiguration. The Carmelites honor him as their spiritual father.
s431.intercession: Holy Elijah, pray for us. Make us zealous for the Lord, and teach us to hear his voice in silence. Amen.

s432.content:
Isaiah prophesied in Jerusalem for some forty years. In the Temple he saw the Lord enthroned and heard the seraphim crying "Holy, holy, holy," and a burning coal touched his lips.

His book foretells the son called Immanuel, whose birth St. Matthew sees fulfilled in the virgin birth of Jesus, the child whose name is Wonderful Counselor, and the Suffering Servant wounded for our transgressions. The Fathers called him the "fifth evangelist," because he speaks so clearly of Christ.
s432.intercession: Holy Isaiah, pray for us. Purify our lips to praise the Holy One, and help us to say, "Here am I! Send me." Amen.

s433.content:
David was the youngest son of Jesse, a shepherd boy anointed by the prophet Samuel, who defeated Goliath and became king of Israel. He made Jerusalem his capital and brought the Ark of the Covenant there with dancing and song.

He sinned gravely with Bathsheba, but repented with his whole heart, and the Psalms traditionally ascribed to him have taught the Church to pray for three thousand years. God promised him a son whose kingdom would have no end, and Jesus is hailed as the Son of David.
s433.intercession: Holy David, pray for us. Teach us to praise God in all things and to repent with a contrite heart. Amen.

s434.content:
When Mary and Joseph brought the infant Jesus to the Temple forty days after his birth, the righteous old man Simeon took him in his arms. The Holy Spirit had promised that he would not die before seeing the Lord’s Christ, and he sang the canticle "Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace."

The prophetess Anna, a widow of great age who never left the Temple, came up at that very hour, gave thanks to God, and spoke of the child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem. The East calls Simeon "the God-Receiver."
s434.intercession: Holy Simeon and Anna, pray for us. Teach us to wait for the Lord with patient hope, and to recognize him when he comes. Amen.

s435.content:
Tradition gives the name Longinus to the Roman soldier who pierced the side of the crucified Christ with a lance, so that blood and water flowed out, and to the centurion at the foot of the Cross who confessed, "Truly this man was the Son of God!"

According to tradition he became a Christian, preached the faith, and died a martyr. A great statue of him by Bernini stands beneath the dome of St. Peter’s Basilica.
s435.intercession: St. Longinus, pray for us. Open our eyes to see who Jesus is, and to confess him without fear. Amen.

s436.content:
In the Gospel of John, Jesus asks a Samaritan woman for a drink at Jacob’s well and offers her living water. Seeing that he knows everything she ever did, she runs back to her town and tells everyone, and many Samaritans believe in him because of her word.

The Eastern tradition calls her Photini, "the enlightened one," and honors her as "equal to the apostles," saying that she preached the Gospel after Pentecost and died a martyr under Nero.
s436.intercession: St. Photini, pray for us. Help us to drink the living water Jesus offers, and to bring others to him. Amen.

s437.content:
According to the ancient Acts of Paul and Thecla, Thecla was a young woman of Iconium who heard St. Paul preach and gave up her engagement to follow Christ. She was condemned to be burned and then thrown to wild beasts, but was miraculously spared each time.

The story was loved in the early Church, and her shrine at Seleucia was a great place of pilgrimage. The Eastern Churches honor her as the first woman martyr and "equal to the apostles."
s437.intercession: St. Thecla, pray for us. Give us courage to follow Christ wholeheartedly, whatever it costs. Amen.

s438.content:
Forty Christian soldiers of the Roman Twelfth Legion at Sebaste in Armenia refused to sacrifice to the pagan gods. They were stripped and left to freeze to death on a frozen lake, with a warm bathhouse on the shore for anyone who would deny Christ.

One soldier gave up and ran to the bath, but a guard who saw a vision of crowns descending on the martyrs took off his armor and joined them, keeping their number at forty. St. Basil the Great preached a famous sermon in their honor.
s438.intercession: Holy Forty Martyrs, pray for us. Strengthen us to stand firm together in the faith until the end. Amen.

s439.content:
Euphemia was a young Christian woman of Chalcedon, near Constantinople, who was martyred during the persecution of Diocletian after refusing to sacrifice to idols.

The Council of Chalcedon met in her basilica in 451. According to a later tradition, the bishops placed the rival statements of faith in her tomb, and the Orthodox one was found in her hand. She is honored as "the all-praised."
s439.intercession: St. Euphemia, pray for us. Help us to hold fast to the true faith about Christ. Amen.

s440.content:
Tatiana was the daughter of a Roman official who secretly raised her as a Christian. According to tradition, she served as a deaconess in Rome and was tortured and martyred under the emperor Alexander Severus.

She is much loved in Russia and Ukraine, where her feast, Tatiana Day, is a holiday for university students.
s440.intercession: St. Tatiana, pray for us. Bless all students, and help them to grow in wisdom and faith. Amen.
